headline: Generative models steer biomolecular design via alignment, energy biasing, and sampling
label: Generative Biomolecular Design Models
summary: Recent preprints extend generative protein and biomolecule models toward steered design, conformational ensembles, and D-peptide targets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is generative or learned sampling of biomolecular structure and sequence, and the newer element is explicit control over that generation. Metadiffusion adds inference-time meta-energy biasing to pretrained biomolecular diffusion models to produce diverse conformational ensembles. A discrete protein diffusion study of antibody design analyzes DPO alignment, reporting that structure aligns early while properties improve slowly, along with collapse mechanisms. Reading TEA leaves scores Metropolis sampling with a 20-letter alphabet derived from protein language model embeddings. Cross-Chirality Generalization injects axial features into E(3)-equivariant vectors so L-L training transfers to latent-diffusion D-peptide design. Structure prediction work (IntelliFold-2, NbForge) and PRIZM's low-N selection of zero-shot models sit adjacent to this thread. CTMD metadynamics addresses docking-hit enrichment through physics-based sampling rather than generative modeling.
